status.label: Win+L is a protected Windows shortcut
status.detail: Windows handles Win+L before Keyboard Manager can remap it; related closed issues #18779 and #15473 document the same protected-combination limitation.

judgment.rationale: The report asks Keyboard Manager to make Caps Lock mapped to Win invoke Win+L, but Windows reserves Win+L to lock the session before Keyboard Manager can process the remapped combination. Maintainer responses on closed issues #18779 and #15473 explicitly document this protected-key-combination limitation. The report also says other Win shortcuts such as Win+M work, which is consistent with the specific Win+L restriction rather than a general remapping failure.
evidence: The reporter uses PowerToys 0.94.0 and maps Caps Lock to Win(left) on an IBM Model M keyboard.
The report says Win+M works but Win+L does not.
Closed issue #18779 has a maintainer explanation that Windows built-in functions such as Win+L are checked before Keyboard Manager.
Closed issue #15473 records that Win+L is a protected key combination.
judgment.recommended_action: Keep the documented Win+L limitation; no Keyboard Manager code change is proposed for this expected protected-key behavior.

fix_assessment.rationale: The requested remapped Win+L behavior is blocked by Windows handling a protected system shortcut before Keyboard Manager. The related closed reports document this limitation, so a PowerToys code fix is not applicable.

issue_context.summary: A Caps Lock-to-Win remap does not make Win+L lock the system, while the reporter says other Win shortcuts work.
known_information: The report lists PowerToys 0.94.0 on Windows 11.
The reporter maps Caps Lock to Win(left) and reports Win+M works but Win+L does not.
Maintainer responses on closed issues #18779 and #15473 state that Win+L is handled or protected by Windows before Keyboard Manager can remap it.
inferences: The observed behavior is consistent with the documented protected shortcut limitation rather than a general failure of the Caps Lock-to-Win mapping.
issue_context.analysis: The exact expected behavior conflicts with the documented Win+L limitation. The report does not establish a separate failure in other remapped Win shortcuts, so no competing fix or new diagnostic request is justified.
